questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 23 protects a person against forced labour imposed by private individuals as well as by the State.
2. Article 23 permits the State to impose compulsory service for public purposes, without discrimination only on grounds of religion, race, caste or class.
3. Article 23 is available only to citizens of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 23 is a right against both State and private persons, and clause (2) lets the State impose compulsory service (such as national service) for public purposes. It is available to all persons, not only citizens, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.h: Art 23 = 'all persons', so foreigners are covered too.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in any employment whatsoever.
2. Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in a factory, a mine or any other hazardous employment.
3. The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, as amended in 2016, prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in all occupations, with limited exceptions such as family enterprises outside school hours.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The constitutional ban in Article 24 is limited to factories, mines and hazardous work, so statement 1 over-generalises. The 2016 amendment to the 1986 Act went further than the Constitution and banned child work in all occupations, with exceptions for family enterprises and child artists.

questions.q:
Statement-I: According to the Supreme Court in the Asiad workers case (PUDR v. Union of India), payment of wages below the minimum wage can amount to 'forced labour' under Article 23.
Statement-II: Article 23 prohibits labour obtained through force, including economic compulsion, even when some remuneration is paid.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Court read 'force' widely: a worker who accepts less than minimum wages out of economic helplessness is compelled, so the labour is forced even though paid. Statement-II gives exactly the reasoning behind Statement-I.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 7 (Fundamental Rights); PUDR v UoI (1982)

questions.q: The right to freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practise and propagate religion under Article 25 is available to
o: citizens and persons of Indian origin only
all persons, citizens and non-citizens alike
questions.e: Article 25 begins 'all persons are equally entitled', so foreigners resident in India enjoy it too. It is not confined to citizens or to minorities.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The wearing and carrying of kirpans is deemed to be included in the profession of the Sikh religion under Article 25.
2. Article 25(2)(b) allows the State to throw open Hindu religious institutions of a public character to all classes and sections of Hindus.
3. For the purposes of Article 25, the reference to Hindus does not include Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Explanation I to Article 25 deems kirpans part of Sikh religion and Explanation II says 'Hindus' includes persons professing Sikh, Jain or Buddhist religion when reading the social-reform clause. Statement 3 states the reverse.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 25 is subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III.
2. Article 26 is subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III.
3. Article 25 guarantees rights to individuals, whereas Article 26 guarantees rights to religious denominations or sections thereof.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 25 is subject also to the other provisions of Part III, so it can be read down by other rights such as Article 14. Article 26 is subject only to public order, morality and health; this subtle difference makes statement 2 wrong.
questions.h: 25 = person + 'other Part III'; 26 = group + only the big three.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a right of a religious denomination under Article 26?
o: To freely profess, practise and propagate religion
To establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes
To manage its own affairs in matters of religion
To own and acquire movable and immovable property and administer it in accordance with law
questions.e: The right to profess, practise and propagate religion is the individual right in Article 25. Article 26 gives the denomination four collective rights: institutions, managing religious affairs, owning property and administering it by law.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Article 27 does not prevent the State from levying a fee on religious institutions for supervising their administration.
Statement-II: Article 27 prohibits only the compulsory payment of taxes whose proceeds are specifically appropriated for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A fee is a payment for a service rendered (here supervision), not a tax, and Article 27 bars only taxes earmarked for a particular religion. This tax-versus-fee distinction was drawn in the Shirur Mutt case.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. No religious instruction can be provided in an educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
2. Religious instruction is permitted in an institution administered by the State but established under an endowment or trust requiring such instruction.
3. A person attending an institution receiving State aid can be compelled to attend religious instruction if the institution's managers insist.
4. No person attending an educational institution recognised by the State can be required to take part in religious worship without his consent.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 28 bans religious instruction in wholly State-funded institutions, permits it in trust-based State-administered ones, and makes attendance voluntary in aided or recognised institutions. Statement 3 contradicts the voluntary-attendance rule.

questions.q: The doctrine of 'essential religious practices', used by courts to decide what is protected under Articles 25 and 26, was first evolved by the Supreme Court in
questions.e: In Commissioner, Hindu Religious Endowments, Madras v. Lakshmindra Thirtha Swamiar of Shirur Mutt, the Court held that what is an essential part of a religion is to be determined by the doctrines of that religion itself. Champakam dealt with communal reservation, Bommai with secularism and federalism.

questions.q: In Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala (1986), the Supreme Court held that
o: students can be expelled from school for refusing to sing the national anthem as it violates the Fundamental Duty to respect it
the national anthem can be made compulsory in all educational institutions under Article 51A(a)
religious faith can never be a ground for exemption from any State-prescribed ritual
students belonging to Jehovah's Witnesses could not be compelled to sing the national anthem when it was against their religious faith, as they stood respectfully while it was sung
questions.e: The Court found no law compelling anyone to sing the anthem and said that expelling the children violated their freedom of speech and expression and freedom of conscience under Articles 19(1)(a) and 25. Respectful silence while the anthem was sung did not insult it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 29(1) is available only to minority communities.
2. Article 29(2) protects an individual citizen, whether belonging to a majority or a minority, from denial of admission to State-maintained or State-aided institutions on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language.
3. Article 30(1) confers on religious and linguistic minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 29(1) speaks of 'any section of citizens' with a distinct language, script or culture, so it can also be used by a section of the majority; it is not confined to minorities. Article 29(2) is an individual right, while Article 30(1) is the minority-specific right.

questions.q: The First Amendment Act 1951 inserted Article 15(4) mainly as a consequence of the judgment in
o: Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar, which struck down zamindari abolition
Golaknath v. State of Punjab, which restricted amendment of Fundamental Rights
Minerva Mills v. Union of India, which restored the balance with Directive Principles
State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan, which struck down a communal order for seats in medical and engineering colleges
questions.e: The Madras communal Government Order reserved college seats by caste and was held to violate Article 29(2). Parliament responded within months by adding Article 15(4) so that the State could make special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes.
questions.h: Champakam -> Clause 4: seats struck, backward-class clause added.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 30(1A), inserted by the 44th Amendment, protects the compensation payable for compulsory acquisition of property of a minority educational institution.
2. Under Article 30(2), the State shall not discriminate against an educational institution in granting aid on the ground that it is managed by a minority.
3. Article 30(1A) was inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from Part III. Because compensation would then no longer be guaranteed for minority institutions, it inserted Article 30(1A) to ensure the amount fixed does not restrict their right. Statement 3 names the wrong amendment.

questions.q: In the T.M.A. Pai Foundation case (2002), the Supreme Court held that for determining who is a minority under Article 30, the unit should be
o: the State, and not the whole of India
the whole of India, for both religious and linguistic minorities
the district in which the institution is located
the Union Territory or State, but only for linguistic minorities
questions.e: The Court said that since States were reorganised on a linguistic basis, a minority, linguistic or religious, must be determined with reference to the State in which the institution is sought to be established.

questions.q:
Which of the following communities have been notified as minority communities at the national level under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992?
1. Zoroastrians (Parsis)
2. Jains
3. Bahais
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Zoroastrians were notified in 1993 and Jains were added in 2014, making six notified communities. Bahais are not notified.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Amendment — Provision
1. First Amendment — Insertion of the Ninth Schedule
2. Fourth Amendment — Insertion of Article 31C
3. Twenty-fifth Amendment — Insertion of Article 31C
4. Forty-second Amendment — Removal of the right to property from Part III
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The First Amendment added Articles 31A and 31B with the Ninth Schedule, and the 25th Amendment (1971) added Article 31C giving primacy to Articles 39(b) and (c). The right to property was removed from Part III by the 44th Amendment (1978), not the 42nd.

questions.q:
With reference to the I.R. Coelho case (2007), consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court held that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review.
2. The test for such review is whether the law violates Part III rights that form part of the basic structure.
3. The Court held that Article 31B completely bars judicial review of all laws placed in the Ninth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: 24 April 1973 is the date of Kesavananda Bharati. Coelho held that Ninth Schedule laws added after that date can be tested against fundamental rights that form part of the basic structure. Immunity under Article 31B is therefore not absolute.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. After the 44th Amendment, the right to property is a constitutional right under Article 300A.
2. Under Article 300A, no person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law.
3. The right to hold, acquire and dispose of property continues to be guaranteed under Article 19(1)(f).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 44th Amendment deleted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and inserted Article 300A in Part XII. Property is now only a legal or constitutional right, so a violation attracts a High Court petition under Article 226 and not a writ under Article 32.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Article 31A protects laws providing for acquisition of estates from challenge on grounds of violating Articles 14 and 19.
Statement-II: Several land reform and zamindari abolition laws had been struck down by courts as violating the right to property and equality, which led Parliament to enact the First Amendment.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Land reforms were stalled by court challenges, so the First Amendment added Articles 31A and 31B to shield agrarian reform laws. Statement-II supplies the cause of the protection described in Statement-I.

questions.q: Article 31C, inserted by the 25th Amendment Act 1971, gave primacy over certain fundamental rights to laws implementing which Directive Principles?
questions.e: Article 31C protects laws meant to secure that ownership of material resources subserves the common good and that wealth does not concentrate. The 42nd Amendment tried to extend this to all Directive Principles, but Minerva Mills struck that extension down.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right.
2. The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is wider than that of the High Courts under Article 226.
3. High Courts can issue writs for the enforcement of ordinary legal rights as well.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 226 lets a High Court issue writs 'for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose', so its jurisdiction is wider than the Supreme Court's, which is limited to Fundamental Rights. Statement 2 reverses this.

questions.q:
Statement-I: A High Court has a wider writ jurisdiction than the Supreme Court.
Statement-II: Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The phrase 'for any other purpose' lets High Courts protect ordinary legal rights, which the Supreme Court cannot do under Article 32. This is the reason for the wider jurisdiction.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A writ of habeas corpus can be issued against a private individual.
2. A habeas corpus petition can be filed by a person other than the detained person.
3. A writ of habeas corpus will lie where a person is detained under an order of a competent court after conviction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Habeas corpus ('to have the body') lies against public authorities and private persons, and a friend or relative can move the court. It will not be issued where detention is by a competent court's lawful order, in contempt proceedings, or outside the court's jurisdiction.

questions.q:
A writ of mandamus cannot be issued against which of the following?
1. The President of India
2. A State Governor
3. The Chief Justice of a High Court acting in a judicial capacity
4. A municipal corporation that fails to perform a mandatory statutory duty
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Mandamus ('we command') compels a public authority to perform its legal duty, but not against the President, Governors or a High Court Chief Justice acting judicially. A municipal corporation neglecting a statutory duty is a classic target for it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Prohibition is issued while proceedings are pending before a lower court or tribunal, whereas certiorari is issued after the order has been passed.
2. Prohibition can be issued against administrative authorities and legislative bodies.
3. Since 1991, certiorari can be issued even against administrative authorities that affect the rights of individuals.
4. Certiorari can never be issued against an administrative authority.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Prohibition is preventive and certiorari is curative. Prohibition lies only against judicial and quasi-judicial bodies, not against administrative or legislative ones, while the Supreme Court extended certiorari to administrative authorities in 1991, so statements 2 and 4 fail.
questions.h: Prohibition = stop before; Certiorari = quash after.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The writ of quo warranto can be sought by any interested person, not only the person whose right is affected.
2. It can be issued in respect of a ministerial or a private office.
3. It can be issued only in the case of a substantive public office of a permanent character created by statute or the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Quo warranto ('by what authority') tests the legality of a person's claim to a public office. Unlike other writs, any interested person may seek it, but it does not apply to private or ministerial offices.

questions.q:
Match List-I (writ) with List-II (meaning of the Latin term):
List-I
A. Habeas corpus
B. Mandamus
C. Certiorari
D. Quo warranto
List-II
1. We command
2. To be certified
3. To have the body
4. By what authority
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Habeas corpus means 'to have the body', mandamus 'we command', certiorari 'to be certified or informed', and quo warranto 'by what authority'. Prohibition means 'to forbid'.

questions.q: A petition is filed challenging the appointment of a person as Vice-Chancellor of a State university on the ground that he does not possess the qualifications prescribed in the University Act. The most appropriate writ is
questions.e: The question is whether the appointee has legal authority to hold a public office created by statute, which is the function of quo warranto. Mandamus enforces a duty, and prohibition stops a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction.

questions.q:
Article 33 empowers Parliament to restrict or abrogate the Fundamental Rights of which of the following?
1. Members of the Armed Forces
2. Members of forces charged with the maintenance of public order
3. Persons employed in intelligence or counter-intelligence organisations
4. Employees of public sector undertakings
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Article 33 aims at ensuring proper discharge of duties and maintenance of discipline in these services. Public sector employees are not covered. Only Parliament, not State legislatures, can make such a law.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 34 provides for restriction of Fundamental Rights while martial law is in force in any area.
2. The term 'martial law' is defined in detail in the Constitution.
3. Under Article 35, State legislatures have the exclusive power to make laws for punishing acts declared offences under Part III.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 34 lets Parliament indemnify officials for acts done during martial law, but the Constitution does not define the term. Under Article 35 it is Parliament, not States, which has exclusive power to make laws on such matters, to ensure uniformity across the country.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Law — Constitutional provision it gives effect to
1. Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 — Article 23
2. Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 — Article 23
3. Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 — Article 24
4. Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 — Article 24
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Bonded Labour and Immoral Traffic Acts implement the bar on forced labour and trafficking in Article 23, and the Child Labour Act implements Article 24. The 2009 Act gives effect to Article 21A (education), not Article 24.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In Rev. Stainislaus v. State of Madhya Pradesh (1977), the Supreme Court held that the right to 'propagate' religion under Article 25 does not include a right to convert another person.
2. Article 25(2)(a) allows the State to regulate economic, financial, political or other secular activity associated with religious practice.
3. Article 25 protects only the religious practices of the majority community.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court said that propagation means transmitting or spreading one's religion by exposition of its tenets, not forcible or fraudulent conversion. The State may regulate secular activity linked to religion, and Article 25 protects all persons of all faiths.

questions.q: Which one of the following grounds is NOT mentioned in Article 29(2) as a ground for denying a citizen admission to an educational institution maintained or aided by the State?
questions.e: Article 29(2) lists religion, race, caste, language or any of them. Place of birth and sex appear in Article 15 but not in Article 29(2).

questions.q:
Arrange the following cases in chronological order:
A. Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala
B. State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
C. T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
D. Rev. Stainislaus v. State of Madhya Pradesh
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Champakam was decided in 1951, Stainislaus in 1977, Bijoe Emmanuel in 1986 and T.M.A. Pai in 2002.

questions.q: Who among the following described the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) as 'the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'?
questions.e: Dr Ambedkar said Article 32 is the heart and soul of the Constitution because without it the other fundamental rights would be mere declarations.

questions.q: Which one of the following Fundamental Rights is available only to citizens of India?
o: Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour (Article 23)
Prohibition of employment of children in hazardous work (Article 24)
Freedom of conscience and free profession of religion (Article 25)
questions.e: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30 are largely citizen-specific, whereas Articles 14, 20 to 28 are available to all persons. Articles 23 to 25 are thus available to foreigners too.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Minorities Commission was initially set up in 1978 by a resolution of the Government of India and was non-statutory.
2. The National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992 gave it statutory status.
3. The National Commission for Minorities has constitutional status under Article 338B.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Commission began as an executive body under a 1978 resolution and became statutory in 1992. Article 338B is the provision for the National Commission for Backward Classes (102nd Amendment), not for minorities.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 350A directs every State to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children belonging to linguistic minorities.
2. The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B is appointed by the Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities.
3. The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities reports to the President, who lays the reports before each House of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Seventh Amendment (1956) added Article 350B; the Officer is appointed by the President and reports to the President, who places the reports before Parliament and sends them to the States.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 15(5) was inserted by the 93rd Amendment Act 2005.
2. It enables the State to make special provisions for admission to educational institutions including private unaided ones, other than minority educational institutions.
3. It applies equally to minority educational institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 93rd Amendment enabled reservation for SC, ST and backward classes in private educational institutions but expressly excluded minority institutions covered by Article 30(1), which protects their right to administer.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty listed in Article 51A?
o: To pay taxes honestly and on time
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform
To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife
questions.e: Paying taxes honestly is a social expectation but it is not listed in Article 51A. The other three are Duties (i), (h) and (g).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fundamental Duties are placed in Part IVA of the Constitution.
2. Article 51A is the only Article in Part IVA.
3. The 86th Amendment Act 2002 added the eleventh Fundamental Duty.
4. Fundamental Duties formed part of the Constitution as originally adopted in 1950.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Part IVA with Article 51A, then containing ten duties. The 86th Amendment (2002) added the duty of parents and guardians in clause (k). The original Constitution had no Fundamental Duties, so statement 4 is false.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable.
2. Fundamental Duties apply to foreigners resident in India as well as to citizens.
3. The Constitution itself does not provide for any sanction for their violation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 51A begins 'it shall be the duty of every citizen of India', so duties bind citizens only, unlike many rights that extend to all persons. Duties cannot be enforced by courts and Part IVA prescribes no punishment.

questions.q: The 86th Amendment Act 2002 added a Fundamental Duty requiring a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the ages of
questions.e: Along with Article 21A (right to education for 6 to 14) and a changed Article 45 (early childhood care for children up to 6), Article 51A(k) places a duty on the parent matching the State's duty.
questions.h: 21A right, 45 below six, 51A(k) parent: all in one 2002 package.

questions.q:
Match List-I (clause of Article 51A) with List-II (Fundamental Duty):
List-I
A. 51A(e)
B. 51A(g)
C. 51A(h)
D. 51A(j)
List-II
1. Develop scientific temper, humanism and spirit of inquiry and reform
2. Protect and improve the natural environment and have compassion for living creatures
3. Strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
4. Promote harmony and renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Clause (e) is on harmony and women's dignity, (g) on the environment, (h) on scientific temper and (j) on excellence.

questions.q: Which one of the following laws deals with insult to the National Flag, the Constitution of India and the National Anthem?
o: Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950
Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
questions.e: The Justice J.S. Verma Committee on Fundamental Duties identified this Act as giving legal effect to the duty to respect the Constitution, the Flag and the Anthem. The Emblems Act of 1950 deals with misuse of official emblems and names.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Fundamental Duties cannot be enforced against a citizen by a writ from a court.
Statement-II: Part IVA of the Constitution does not provide for any legal sanction for the violation of the Fundamental Duties.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Without a legal sanction, there is nothing a court can enforce directly. Parliament may, however, make specific laws to enforce a particular duty, such as the 1971 Act on national honour.

questions.q: The idea of incorporating Fundamental Duties in the Constitution was inspired by the Constitution of
questions.e: The Swaran Singh Committee recommended duties in 1976, and the framers of the 42nd Amendment drew upon the USSR Constitution, which listed rights alongside duties. The USA and Ireland contributed other features such as fundamental rights and Directive Principles.

questions.q: A group of citizens voluntarily clean a polluted lake, plant trees on its bank and rescue stray animals injured by traffic. Which Fundamental Duty are they primarily performing?
questions.e: Clause (g) mandates protecting and improving the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and having compassion for living creatures. Clause (i) concerns public property and violence.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended that penalties or punishment should be prescribed for non-compliance with Fundamental Duties.
Statement-II: The 42nd Amendment Act incorporated penal provisions for the violation of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Committee did suggest that Parliament should provide for penalties, but this recommendation was not accepted. The 42nd Amendment added only the list of duties, with no punishment.
